alt: Three needs: achievement (succeeding at challenging tasks, preferring moderately difficult goals and feedback), affiliation (being liked, preferring cooperation) and power (influencing others). A manager can give a high-achievement employee a target-based project and a high-affiliation employee a team role. Projective measures limit reliability.
caption: Three learned needs; match each employee's role to their strongest one.

alt: Five goal-setting principles: clarity, challenge, commitment, feedback and task complexity. Below, a vague goal ("Improve customer service") is turned into a SMART goal ("Answer 90% of customer emails within 24 hours by the end of March").
caption: Turn vague aims into specific, measurable, time-bound goals.

alt: A table compares need theories (Maslow, McClelland: what motivates, unmet needs, more deterministic) with cognitive theories (goal-setting, VIE: how motivation is produced, goals and beliefs, an active worker).
caption: Need theories explain what motivates; cognitive theories explain how.

alt: Extrinsic motivators (pay, bonus, profit-sharing, performance-related pay) and intrinsic motivators (praise, respect, recognition, empowerment, belonging). Self-determination theory's three needs, competence, autonomy and relatedness, follow; informational rewards can support intrinsic motivation while controlling rewards can undermine it.
caption: The same reward can support or undermine motivation depending on how it feels.
